title: Graceful Degradation Orchestrator: automatic fallback & circuit-breaker policy for regional/tier routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a Graceful Degradation Orchestrator (GDO) to the request router to automatically trigger fallbacks and circuit breakers based on 429s, timeouts, and error-rate thresholds across region and customer tier. The GDO should support per-region and per-tier policies, per-model-variant fallbacks, hysteresis, and an emergency bypass for SRE. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout plan for the initial policy set and observability hooks.
background: We frequently see short-lived regional overloads and model-specific regressions causing spikes in 429s and timeouts. Current fallback behavior is manual or coarse-grained; customers experience increased tail latency and degraded UX while engineers triage. A programmable, observable orchestrator will allow automatic, safe failover from an overloaded model/region/tier to alternatives with clear SLAs and audit trails.
proposed_solution: Implement a GDO component within the routing layer that evaluates sliding-window metrics (429 rate, timeout rate, overall error rate, p95/p99 latency) per region-tier-model. Policies are defined as rules with: trigger thresholds, minimum sample window, cooldown period, fallback target(s), and severity (soft/hard). Circuit breaker modes: soft (rate-limited reroute + sampling), hard (full block + fallback). Hysteresis and exponential backoff prevent oscillation. Provide APIs to override or pin behavior for Dedicated/Private customers.
tradeoffs:
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but increase detection latency.
- Per-customer granularity increases memory/metric cardinality; initial rollout will use per-region + per-tier granularity, with opt-in per-customer.
- Soft breakers preserve telemetry and allow partial traffic to test fallbacks; hard breakers minimize blast radius at the cost of more aggressive routing changes.
- Adding logic to the hot routing path increases CPU; we will offload evaluation to a fast in-process evaluator and cache decisions for short TTLs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router exposes a new policy config schema and default policy for hosted API. 2) Automatic fallback triggers when 429_rate >= 5% over 60s OR timeout_rate >= 2% over 60s for a region-tier-model, performing soft fallback first, then hard if escalation rules met. 3) Circuit breaker state visible in Console (per-route/model) with audit trail and recent triggers. 4) No regressive latency on p50/p90 (<5% increase) for normal traffic. 5) Integration tests and chaos-runbook executed and passing.
metrics_and_slos: Primary signals: 429_rate, timeout_rate, error_rate, p99_latency, fallback_rate, rollback_count. SLO goals for rollout: fallback false-positive rate < 1% on controlled traffic, detection-to-fallback latency < 90s for high-severity events, mean time to restore via automated fallback < 3min for region overloads.
implementation_steps: Define policy schema (YAML/JSON) and validation rules
Prototype fast evaluator service (in-router process) with sliding-window counters and decay
Implement fallback executor to reroute to model variants or alternate regions and apply soft/hard modes
Add persistent audit log entries (structured events) for each policy action
Wire metrics (Prometheus) and Console visualization panels
Add feature flags and canary rollout path per region and per-tier
Write integration and load tests; run chaos experiments (5xx/timeout/429 injection)
Document behavior and runbook in Confluence; add SRE escalation steps

rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary in us-west for non-critical routes (2 weeks). 2) Expand to all regions for hosted API after monitoring (3 weeks). 3) Beta opt-in for Dedicated customers with per-customer policies. 4) Gradual enablement for Private installs with config tool. Each step includes a 48-hour watch with SRE and a rollback gate.
qa_and_chaos_tests: Create synthetic traffic patterns with controlled 429/timeouts and validate that GDO triggers soft fallback first and escalates to hard only if thresholds persist. Inject network partitions in a single region and confirm automatic reroute to other regions without data loss. Verify audit logs and UI visibility for each simulated event.
notes: We will prefer model-variant fallbacks that preserve API compatibility (same tokenizer/response schema). For models with incompatible outputs, route to a lightweight fallback chain that returns a graceful degradation response with an error_code field and a hint for clients.
